newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma eases, short depos up, coupon bonds firm.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma eases, short depos up, coupon bonds firm.

text.p: Greek depos nudged higher a tenth of a point in short tenors, forex forwards were trading narrowly, taxable coupon bonds were firmer and ecu/drachma was easier around mid-session, traders said.
"Short-term depos trade higher 10 basis points on a reallocation of funds among banks," said a dealer at a private bank. "Overall, interbank liquidity has not changed much."
The dealer said forex forwards were little changed and the market was quiet.
The central bank offered to drain up to 200 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular competitive interest rate tender.
"I expect the tender's allotment ratio to be smaller today," the dealer said.
The allotment ratio stood at 4.96 percent last Wednesday.
Bond traders said there was buying interest for taxable three-, five- and seven-year coupon bonds pushing prices a few ticks higher.
The mark was quoted at 159.00/10 from Tuesday's 159.035 fix, the dollar at 269.81/91 drachmas from 269.600 and the ecu at 310.40/45 from 310.720 drachmas.
"The drachma is firmer against the ecu trading at 310.40/45 after opening at 310.70/75," said a forex trader at a foreign bank. "We have seen some ecu selling for drachmas."
Asked if stop-losses had been triggered as ecu/drachma was heading down in the last few days, the dealer said this could explain the ecu selling for drachmas from abroad.
"But I do not think there are many guys out there who are silly to be long ecu, short drachma," the trader said.
